requirement:
A definition's reference set MUST consist of its current incoming `{impl}` and
`{test}` edges under {cite}`requirements.references.targets` and
{cite}`requirements.references.anchors`: for each edge, its role and the file and
outline selector of the node the reference belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, or of the anchored file or
node. `{cite}` references MUST NOT contribute. The reference-set digest MUST be
the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of those entries in sorted order,
so it does not depend on line numbers or on the order references are found.
Authoring MUST record the digest of the reference set it supplied, and
validation MUST recompute it and report a changed reference set as stale
evidence. Adding or removing an `{impl}` or `{test}` reference or anchor,
changing its role, or moving it to a different node MUST therefore make the
evidence stale even when no recorded input changed; moving a reference within
the node it belongs to MUST NOT.
rationale:
**Judgment: the requirement is met.** The implementation covers every obligation, and the tests cover the main points of the design space. One small deviation from the spec is noted below.

**Implementation**
- `reference_set_digest` (`src/evidence.rs`) builds the reference set.
  - It keeps only `Impl` and `Test` references whose name matches the definition. `{cite}` references are filtered out, so they do not contribute.
  - Each reference contributes its role, its file, and the selector of the outline node it belongs to. The node comes from `Outline::owner_at_line`, which uses the comment-run ownership of `requirements.references.outline_comments`. Plain-text files, and sources that cannot be outlined, contribute the root selector.
  - Line numbers are never encoded, so moving a reference within its node leaves the digest unchanged.
  - Anchors from `definition.anchors` contribute their role, file and selector.
  - Entries are sorted before hashing, so discovery order does not matter.
  - The encoding is SHA-256 over a count followed by length-prefixed fields, which makes it unambiguous.
- Authoring records the digest.
  - `AssessmentSources::prepare` computes it, and `assess` writes it to the `references` field of the evidence record.
  - `add_definition_inputs` and `update_inputs` in `src/add_input.rs` record it too. A changed digest resets the determination to false and the rationale to a "Review pending" message even when no input changed.
- Validation recomputes the digest.
  - `validate_references` compares the recorded digest with the current one and reports "reference set changed" as an error.
  - `validate_evidence_file` enforces that `references` is a lowercase hex SHA-256 string.
  - `reference_set_digest_for` is a public helper for recomputing a digest.
- Marking: the `{impl}` references sit on all of these sites.
- Deviation: the encoding includes an extra `origin` field ("reference" or "anchor"). The spec lists only role, file and selector. The effect is that replacing a reference with an anchor to the same node changes the digest. That is conservative, and adding or removing the edge is stale under the spec anyway, so I do not count it as a gap.

**Tests**
- `reference_set_digest_tracks_impl_and_test_edges_by_node` covers:
  - Determinism, and a 64-character hex digest.
  - Invariance: unrelated lines, moves within a node, comment placement within a node, text-file and Markdown line shifts, and `{cite}` additions.
  - Change: adding or removing a reference, re-roling, moving to another node, and Markdown section changes.
  - Anchor changes: `:impl:` and `:test:` on a file, and on a node.
- `validation_requires_a_current_reference_set_digest` covers:
  - A current digest, which passes.
  - A missing, non-string, uppercase or truncated digest, which each give the expected error.
  - A new `{impl}` inside an already-covered node, which gives "reference set changed" while no input hash changed.
- `throttled_requests_retry_unchanged_and_record_every_attempt` and `bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors` verify that authoring records the digest.
- `add_input_requires_one_target_and_mode_and_resets_changed_records` verifies that add-input records the digest, and that a changed reference set resets review even when every input is unchanged.
- `batch_reauthors_a_false_judgment_when_its_reference_set_changes` verifies end to end that a changed reference set makes the record stale and that batch authoring re-authors it.
- Fixture helpers in `tests/outcomes.rs`, `tests/evidence_boundaries.rs` and `src/evidence.rs` keep the other tests consistent.

No acknowledged gaps (FIXMEs) were found.

A definition's reference set MUST consist of its current incoming `{impl}` and
`{test}` edges under {cite}`requirements.references.targets` and

node. `{cite}` references MUST NOT contribute. The reference-set digest MUST be
the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of those entries in sorted order,
so it does not depend on line numbers or on the order references are found.
Authoring MUST record the digest of the reference set it supplied, and
validation MUST recompute it and report a changed reference set as stale
evidence. Adding or removing an `{impl}` or `{test}` reference or anchor,
changing its role, or moving it to a different node MUST therefore make the
evidence stale even when no recorded input changed; moving a reference within
the node it belongs to MUST NOT.
:::{req} targets

Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name. Each reference is a directed edge between its source and the named definition. A source is a project source item or a requirement or example declaration. `{cite}` MUST mean that the source relies on, supports, or refers to the definition, and is an edge from the source to the definition. `{impl}` MUST mean that the source implements part of the definition: it makes a decision, performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case that the definition specifies. A requirement MAY implement part of another requirement by refining one of its obligations. Calling code that implements a definition, or producing a result a caller uses to meet it, MUST NOT by itself count as implementing it. A requirement stating a convention for every output of a kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by the source that carries out the convention as a whole, such as the step that collects and reports those outputs. `{test}` MUST mean that the source is designed to verify behavior the definition specifies: a test through its scenario and the assertions about that scenario's outcome, or a named example through the concrete case it describes. `{impl}` and `{test}` are edges from the definition to the source. Only requirements and examples are assessed; code is reviewed as part of the definitions it implements or tests. Habeas MUST find these references throughout project source files and MUST fail with the source file and line if a name has no matching `{req}` or `{example}` definition. In Markdown, escaped roles and roles in code examples MUST remain literal. Evidence snapshots and generated build output MUST NOT be counted as additional source references: discovery MUST skip `.git` and `target` directories at any depth and the project-root `book` and `evidence` directories.
```text
{impl}`requirements.references.targets`
{cite}`requirements.references.targets`
{test}`requirements.references.targets`
:::{req} anchors
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
`path#selector` for one outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.targets`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.
An anchored file or node MUST be covered by the definition's evidence under
{cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`, by an input selecting it, so changing the file makes that evidence stale. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference, because the
definition cannot be assessed without it. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.
Agents SHOULD NOT anchor a file when a more precise reference is available, such
as a reference attached to the Rust item that implements or tests the
definition. Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST give this direction.
:::{req} outline_comments
Each documented profile defines which grammar nodes are comments; the Markdown
profile's comments are HTML comment blocks, so an inline HTML comment within a
paragraph is text of its section. In every supported language, comments on consecutive lines with no other source
between them MUST form one comment run. A comment that follows other source on
the same line, including another comment, MUST form a run by itself and MUST belong to the innermost outline node
containing that line. Any other run MUST belong to the next outline node that
starts after it within the smallest node containing it; when that container has
no such node, the run MUST belong to the container, which is the root node at top
level. A profile MAY bind a comment kind to its container
instead: such a run MUST belong to the smallest node containing it. The Rust
profile MUST bind inner doc comments (`//!`, `/*!`) to their container, so a
file-level inner doc comment belongs to the root node. A reference in a comment MUST count for the node its run belongs to under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage` and
{cite}`requirements.references.authoring_inputs`.
